source.quote: Burson Audio's own page for the Conductor Voyager, read 2026-11-25. Inputs row: « 2 x XLR | 2 x RCA | USB | Optical Toslink | Bluetooth 5.0 | Microphone ». Rate rows: « PCM Support | PCM <= 768 kHz @ 16, 24 or 32 bits »; « Native DSD 64 / 128 / 256 / 512 »; « DSD over PCM | DoP64 / DoP128 / DoP256 / DoP512 »; « COAX & Toslink / SPDIF | Up to 24 bit 192 kHz ». Body text: « At the heart of the Conductor Voyager is the ESS9039PRO DAC »; « The ESS9039PRO DAC offers 24 filter and path settings »; « USB-C XMOS interface: Supports native DSD512 and 32-bit/786kHz PCM » - the page prints 786, not 768.

facts.chip: « the ESS9039PRO DAC », fed by a « USB-C XMOS interface ».

_verification_des_conditions_tentee_et_N: No terms-of-use, terms-of-service or legal-notice page was found on bursonaudio.com. The home page, the shop, four product pages and the return-and-warranty policy were all read and none links to one; the returns page restricts purchases and says nothing about site content. BUT the reader reports that the footer text was not visible in any extracted page, so a footer link may exist and have been missed. The check was therefore ATTEMPTED AND INCONCLUSIVE, not clean - which is a different thing from Pro-Ject, where the Imprint and the data-protection page were read and cleared. The facts are recorded, because the rule is to integrate unless explicitly forbidden and nothing forbidding was found; the quality of the check is recorded with them, because on 2026-11-25 three makers were refused on clauses that live exactly where this one could not look.
_786_kHz_est_une_coquille_et_768_est_ecr: The body says « 32-bit/786kHz PCM » and the specification row says « PCM <= 768 kHz ». 786 kHz is not a rate that exists - the multiples of 44.1 and 48 run 705.6 and 768 - so it is a transposition, and the Conductor Stellar's page on the same site prints « 768kHz » correctly in the same sentence. 768000 is recorded and the typo is kept in the quote. Worth naming because a reader checking this catalogue against the page will find a figure that does not match, and the reason should not have to be rediscovered.
_deux_entrees_ANALOGIQUES_dans_la_liste_: « 2 x XLR | 2 x RCA » head the input row of a DAC. They are line-level analogue inputs - this device is also a preamplifier - and nothing is written from them. The row is a reminder that a maker's « inputs » list is whatever it chose to put there, and that four of the six entries on this one carry no digital audio at all.
_vingt_quatre_reglages_de_filtre_que_per: « The ESS9039PRO DAC offers 24 filter and path settings ». Twenty-four, the largest count any maker in this catalogue has published, and not one is named - nor does the page say whether the owner can reach them. No device_settings entry. The Topping DX1 II's manual, read the same day, names eight of what is very probably the same chip's menu; this maker states the number as a feature and stops.
